hypothesis: With the streaming of the first experiment, the CPU kernels for multi-row prompts, the fused silu, the vectorized attention scores and the spread o_proj placement, a full MiMo-Pro request runs faster than the measured release engine with byte-identical replies.
model: XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD, all 70 layers, native MXFP4 experts and FP8/BF16 dense
command:
Baseline: the release engine of mimo-cuda-4090-2026-10-16.
Trial:
git checkout 10313e4f
c/build_mimo_cuda.bat
mingw32-make -C c mimo CUDA_DLL=1 ARCH=native VK=0
Both:
python c/tools/benchmark_mimo_cuda.py --engine c/mimo.exe --model D:/AI/Models/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD --shards C:/AI/MiMoPro-Shards --backend cuda --release-host --cap 104 --threads 16 --read-threads 16 --context 16384 --tokens 64 --runs 3 --output <dir>

hardware.ram: 192 GiB installed (4 x 48 GiB), DDR5 configured at 5400 MT/s; 191.08 GiB OS-visible; ~65 GB/s measured read bandwidth
hardware.storage: C: one PCIe 5.0 x4 NVMe (88 shards, ~10.5 GB/s direct 19 MB reads); D: three PCIe 4.0 NVMe striped behind the chipset (42 shards, ~6.5 GB/s); ~17.7 GB/s together. Native Windows unbuffered reads.
hardware.os: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations 10.0.26300; MinGW-w64 GCC 14.2 MSVCRT, MSVC 14.44; RTX 4090 24 GiB WDDM, driver 617.42, CUDA Toolkit 13.2, sm_89

quality.method: Exact arms: every measured reply byte-identical to the release engine's (SHA-256 0305abcd...); full 70-layer CPU logits equal to the release engine's (correctness/).
